_comment: Reference completion hashes for the Qwen3.6-27B champion stack, so that a
reproduction can be checked against OUR result and not merely against
itself. Without this file a reproducer can only prove self-consistency:
run twice, get the same answer, learn nothing about whether it is the same
Each sha is sha256(completion_text)[:16] -- the same value decode_bench.py
writes to its --json-out. Produced at 256 max_tokens, temperature 0,
Confirmed across two independently built binaries and four passes.
IMPORTANT: these hashes are properties of OUR two checkpoints, and neither
is published -- the target is a locally assembled snapshot and the drafter
is an in-house DFlash retrain. If you substitute a public Qwen3.6-27B
DFlash drafter the acceptance changes, so the completions change, so this
file will report MISMATCH on every stable row. That is the correct result
for different weights and is NOT evidence your build is broken. Only run
the checker against a run made on the same two checkpoints. For a decode
reference you can actually check against, use the laguna branch: both of
its checkpoints are public. See README section 1.
Check a run with:  python3 bench/qwen/check_repro.py <json-out file>

champion.description: The champion configuration launched by serve_champion.sh.

prose.note: Intermittently nondeterministic: 3 of 4 observed passes gave the first hash, 1 gave the second. Lowest-acceptance row (1.60/16). Both outputs are fluent and on-topic, diverging mid-sentence into different phrasing rather than into corruption. A mismatch here is NOT evidence your build is wrong. See README section 5.
